rows.sourceEnglish: One bed over three seasons: a fast crop is harvested, then a new sowing goes in beside a slower crop that is still growing, so the bed is never empty.

imageEvidence: Three views arranged left-to-right portray the same bed layout through stages in the canonical interpretation.
First view shows a person harvesting small leafy crops into a basket.
Middle view shows small newly established plants beside larger plants along the other side.
Third view shows fuller growth beside the larger continuing plants; none of the three views is empty.
There are no time labels; exactly three seasons derives from source rather than independently measurable image timing.
The image does not show seed placement itself, so sowing versus generic planting is distinguished by source wording.

semanticCheck.threeSeasons: exact English over three seasons retained
semanticCheck.sequenceBesideContinuedGrowth: harvest, kutani/then, kusuhi/beside, slower crop still growing and never-empty framing retained
semanticCheck.remainingSpecificityRisk: ku byariwa swin'wana is backtranslated by the supplement as something is planted; source says a new sowing. Generic planting can include transplanting and does not explicitly bind the sowing event. The image cannot resolve that wording ambiguity.
semanticCheck.boundedRecommendation: Retain exact new sowing inside the ordinary then/beside framing, or obtain independent exact sowing wording; do not claim the picture proves the generic replacement equivalent.

rows.verdict: diagram correspondence accepted; source-specific new-sowing semantic anchor still merits bounded repair/check before application
